name: Build extraordinary teams
definition: Hold a high bar. Give and seek candid feedback. Build connected, supportive, diverse, and inclusive teams that are greater than the sum of their parts.

terms.label: greater than the sum of their parts

rows.under: Lowers the bar to fill a seat or to keep the peace.
rows.justRight: Holds a high bar for who joins and what ships. Explains the bar so people can meet it.
rows.over: Raises the bar after the fact. Uses it to block people rather than to build the team.

rows.under: Withholds the hard message. Lets weak work pass with a smile.
rows.justRight: Gives candid feedback while it can still change the work. Is specific, timely, and aimed at the outcome.
rows.over: Uses candor as cover for cruelty. Feedback becomes a performance, not a tool.

rows.under: Asks only the people who will agree. Treats critique as disloyalty.
rows.justRight: Seeks candid feedback, including from people who will disagree. Changes course when the feedback is right.
rows.over: Collects so much feedback that no decision lands. Uses the search for input to avoid owning the call.

rows.under: Lets people work in isolation. Does not notice when someone is stuck or excluded.
rows.justRight: Builds a team that is connected and supportive. People know how their work fits, and they help each other over the hard parts.
rows.over: Forces togetherness at the expense of the work. Meetings replace delivery.

rows.situation: Building a diverse and inclusive team
rows.under: Hires in their own image. Does not make space for people who work or think differently.
rows.justRight: Builds diverse and inclusive teams that are stronger than any one person. Different views are used, not just collected.
rows.over: Treats diversity as a slogan. Counts representation and stops before the team actually works as one.
